original_text: A 45-year-old woman presenting with a 10-year history of palpitations and recent aggravation accompanied with dyspnea was referred to our center. She was originally diagnosed with biventricular HCM yet did not receive relevant treatment. Assessment of family medical history revealed that her mother died of a sudden cardiac death (SCD). summary: 45-year-old woman with 10-year history of palpitations and recent dyspnea aggravation referred for evaluation. Previously diagnosed with biventricular HCM without treatment. Family history: mother died of sudden cardiac death. Physical exam: stable vital signs except tachycardia (112 bpm) and loud grade 4/6 systolic ejection murmur.

summary: 15-year-old male with non-transfusion-dependent SCD (hemoglobin SS) on hydroxyurea 1,000 mg daily. Chronic aching pain and limited range of motion in both hips and right shoulder. original_text: A 67-year-old man presented an out-of-hospital episode of syncope during nighttime with convulsive seizures. The history included hypertension and a recently diagnosed prostatic cancer, under treatment with irbesartan, hydrochlorothiazide, and the gonadotrophin-releasing hormone-receptor agonists/antagonists leuprolide (depot formulation: 22.5 mg every 3 months, for several months). He had no family history for SCD. The ECG on admission demonstrated sinus bradycardia and marked QTc prolongation
summary: 67-year-old male presented with out-of-hospital syncope and convulsive seizures. History: hypertension, prostatic cancer (treated with leuprolide, irbesartan, hydrochlorothiazide). No family history of SCD. Admission ECG: sinus bradycardia, marked QTc prolongation.
